\section{Purpose}

This document lists every component needed to build, test and operate
the
three RescueSwarm aircraft and their ground station, with quantities, unit
prices and the supplier each price was taken from. Every price is from a dated
Indian listing, and each supplier name in Section~\ref{sec:bom} links to it,
except the consumables, which are a marked allowance. The totals are the same as
those in the programme brief and the approval letters, because all three are
generated from one parts list.

\section{System configuration}

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}L{3.2cm}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Airframe} & Quadrotor, 18\,in carbon propellers, Tarot 5008 340\,KV motors, carbon-tube arms; about 7\,kg take-off mass with four relief kits \\
\textbf{Flight control} & Holybro Kakute H7 V1.5 running ArduPilot, stacked on a 4-in-1 65\,A speed controller \\

\textbf{Positioning} & Centimetre-level RTK on every aircraft (ZED-F9P, dual-band, with compass); own ground base station, so no internet is needed \\
\textbf{Video} & Digital downlink (wfb-ng) carrying the camera feed with detections drawn on; one directional ground receiver per aircraft \\
\textbf{Links} & 2.4\,GHz ExpressLRS for the safety pilot; 868\,MHz LoRa for RTK corrections \\
\textbf{Power} & 6S 16\,Ah LiHV lithium-polymer pack, charged on the LiHV profile (4.35\,V per cell); AS150 connectors; separate regulators for the computer, the video radio and the servos \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\section{Battery selection}

The battery is the largest single design decision in this parts list. The
previous design used a pack built in-house from eighteen cells. A bought
lithium-polymer pack avoids spot-welding cells in a student lab. It has to be
large enough to keep the mission's energy reserve \emph{after} its own extra
weight is counted, because a heavier aircraft needs more power to hover. Each
candidate was run through the project's sizing model at its own mass:

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrrrr@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Pack} & \textbf{Mass} & \textbf{Energy} & \textbf{Take-off} & \textbf{Thrust/} & \textbf{Endurance} & \textbf{Landing} \\
 & \textbf{kg} & \textbf{Wh} & \textbf{mass, kg} & \textbf{weight} & \textbf{ratio} & \textbf{reserve, Wh} \\
\midrule
Li-ion 6S3P, in-house (previous) & 1.45 & 292 & 6.36 & 2.00 & 2.02 & +1.1 \\
LiPo 12\,Ah & 1.42 & 266 & 6.34 & 2.01 & 1.85$^\ast$ & $-$3.7$^\ast$ \\
LiPo 13\,Ah & 1.52 & 289 & 6.43 & 1.98 & 1.96$^\ast$ & $-$0.5$^\ast$ \\
LiPo 14\,Ah & 1.64 & 311 & 6.55 & 1.94 & 2.06 & +2.5 \\
\textbf{LiPo 16\,Ah LiHV (selected)} & \textbf{1.88--2.21} & \textbf{365} & \textbf{6.8--7.1} & \textbf{1.8--1.9} & \textbf{2.1--2.3} & \textbf{+5 to +9} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

{\footnotesize \emph{Endurance ratio} is hover time divided by mission time; the
design requires at least 2.0. \emph{Landing reserve} is the energy left after the
third aircraft waits its turn and descends, and must be positive. $^\ast$\,Fails
the requirement. The 16\,Ah pack's mass is a range because the maker does not
publish it.\par}

The 12 and 13\,Ah packs fail both requirements, and about 14\,Ah is the smallest
that passes. The 16\,Ah pack is the smallest suitable size on sale in India. Its
cost is weight: on the same motors, thrust-to-weight falls from 2.0 to about
1.8--1.9 unless the thrust stand measures at least 3.55\,kgf per motor. That
measurement is the first gate in Section~\ref{sec:verify}.

\section{Test plan}\label{sec:verify}

The following are checked when the parts arrive or before first flight. Each
is either a measurement this programme exists to make, or a confirmation that
a listing cannot give. \emph{Planned} means the test is scheduled at the stage
shown.

1 & Battery mass & Weigh each pack on receipt. & Expected 1.88--2.21\,kg. The measured mass replaces the estimate in the take-off mass. & On receipt & Planned \\
2 & Motor thrust & Thrust-stand test of one motor, propeller and speed controller. & $\geq$\,3.55\,kgf per motor, which keeps thrust-to-weight at 2.0 at the heaviest expected mass. & Phase 2 & Planned \\
3 & Pack fuse & Log peak current on the stand and in the first flights. & The 150\,A fuse must hold against a $\sim$136\,A peak. This is the tightest electrical margin. & Phase 2 & Planned \\
4 & Battery failsafe & Loaded discharge of the received pack at hover current. & Failsafe parameters are set for the 16\,Ah LiPo (land with 20\,\% left). The discharge confirms the voltage backstop fires near 20\,\%. \textbf{No flight before this is done.} & Before first flight & Planned \\

Measure the range on our own link, not the listing's analog-FPV figure. Set coax lengths from the station layout. & Ground-station build & Planned \\

\section{Basis of prices}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=14pt,itemsep=1pt,topsep=2pt]
\item Prices were taken from Indian supplier listings on 19--20 September 2026. Where
      a supplier blocked automated checking, the same part's price at another
      Indian retailer was used, and that retailer is the one linked.
\item Retail listings already include GST and are used as listed. Pre-GST quotations,
      B2B listings and estimates have 18\,\% GST added (\rs{2{,}650}).
\item A 15\,\% contingency is applied to the whole, for price movement between
      now and each phase's purchase.
\item Customs duty does not apply: every part is bought from a supplier in India.
\end{itemize}
